text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key idea is following naming conventions: use clear, meaningful names for variables and functions, so others can quickly see what they do. Another important point is keeping functions small and focused on one task. This makes code easier to test and reuse. Finally, clean code is easier to maintain. When you need to fix a bug or add a feature later, well-organized code saves time and reduces mistakes. In short, writing clean code helps both you and your team work more efficiently.
